summary.title: Web Application Security Guide/Checklist
summary.one_liner: A checklist of common web application security pitfalls and the defenses to apply against each, covering injection, XSS, CSRF, uploads, sessions, TLS and password storage.
takeaways: Validate all input server side, treating POST/GET data, cookies, headers and the request URL as untrusted.
Prevent SQL injection with prepared statements or stored procedures and give the DB account minimal rights.
Escape output for its specific context (HTML, attribute, JavaScript, CSS, headers) as close to output as possible, and use a CSRF token plus X-Frame-Options against CSRF and clickjacking.
Harden sessions and passwords: regenerate session IDs at login, set HttpOnly and secure cookies, store passwords only as salted, slow hashes such as Argon2, scrypt or bcrypt.
summary.summary: This Wikibooks page is a flat checklist rather than a tutorial, organized by vulnerability class: file inclusion, file upload, SQL injection, XSS, XML and API security, CSRF, clickjacking, insecure transport, session fixation and stealing, truncation, password storage, comparison pitfalls, and PHP-specific hardening. Each section lists short imperative rules with brief rationale, sometimes naming specific headers, libraries or PHP settings. It includes a few dated recommendations (for example, a 2048-bit key length described as usual in 2013), so some specifics may be outdated. It is useful as a quick review list rather than a step-by-step guide.
